item.title: Re: Shepherd boy
item.content:encoded:
Oh how I wish I could greenlight this, but I can't so instead I'll give my two cents!

I love this, it's exactly what I look for in an article. There are so many questions, with some answers but not so many that it becomes fully explained and boring.

They wander the place until they found wast space with what it seemed to be a ger (Yurt) in the middle and behind that was a dozen branch people1 facing the sky. they travel through the crowd and Agent Olson loses two agents among them.

This dot point alone is perhaps one of the most intriguing parts of the narrative (to me at least). What are these branch people? What happened to their fellow MTF? Pondering these details are super fun.

And the idea of a fairytale turned prophecy is refreshing. I do worry if you will be able to pull this off, but you definitely have a solid concept!

Dr Narangerel interviewed the entity and found out it has home which was an cave underneath a destroyed mining factory.

How does this interview happen? There's kinda a jump from "we sent a research team to find out what the SCP is" to "we interviewed it" and I'm not sure how you're like…getting from A to B here?

My kinda concern here is this feels like a lot of preamble that's not hugely interesting when the real meat is the MTF team exploring the cave; and it feels like just a handwave 'locals claim the cave is haunted' in a discovery section would be the best way to convey this so you can go from giving vague description of entity to the actual exploration log that's the real joy here as quick as possible?

I'm a little unclear on why they have no choice but to go down further. The snake attack kinda feels like a 'go back now' kinda action so it seems like it shouldn't be blocking their access but?

they travel through the crowd and Agent Olson loses two agent among them.

How does Olson lose two agents here? The phrasing is kinda vague but it seems like there's some kinda cognitohazardous affect here forcing people to give worship? But it also seems plausible that there's just, the sinkhole thing at play here?

item.title: Re: Shepherd boy
item.content:encoded:
at first i thought about making it an investigate format story about trying crack this SCP about its origins and the reason why it goes around attacking mining factories

This is actually something you'll want to focus on no matter what you do with this; an entity that attacks mining facilities is a generic monster. An entity with an origin grounded in the mythology of the region that has an understandable reason for attacking mining facilities (preferably with some unexpected twists along the way) is a character.

Specifically, I'd focus on the aspect of what turns this entity against the mines- it's fairly easy to have it simply be angry about the mining boom in Mongolia, but what if it's not about the mines per-say? In the days of the Khans, Mongolia was the largest empire on Earth, and today those mines have the potential to return a measure of that glory- provided Mongolia isn't cut out of its own harvest.

Iunno: at the end of the day, I have some concerns but mostly I just want to see that you know the rough shape of this as a full story.

item.title: Shepherd boy
item.content:encoded:
seeking to greenlight: yes

Page Type: SCP article

Page layout: Interview log and Body cam

Genre: Mystery

Elevator pitch: This SCP is a Mongolian (Khun) teenage boy that can manipulate any natural structure and can create a giant creature that is a snake. However, it can't manifest creatures if it nor surrounded by any natural habitats, is incredibly sensitive to fire.
there's SCP-1 where it is a hole in a destroyed mining factory leading down to a cave. And it seems the anomaly is protecting the cave.

+ Central Narrative
- Central Narrative

After mass death and disappearance of local cattle and animals. And destruction major mining factory The Foundation dispatched a research team to try to find out what this SCP is. they found out that this SCP is known among the locals as a fairy tale and folklore making it alive since the Khun era. They learned from the locals that there was a huge abandoned mining factory somewhere near the district, saying it has some kind of presence.

  • MTF- Zeta-9 with average equipment and firearms for the exploratory mission. team leader Olson. Agent Luna, Ouyulan, Zachary, and Sunder.
  • they're communication completely cuts off once they enter the dark zone, they shine a light and saw a snake-like creature big as skyscrapers on the walls. the cave expands, as further they go, and the light gradually returns, revealing a whole echo system with animal same as above but made out of natural components.
  • the snake attacks the team. Zachary and Ouyulan are eaten, the remaining three had no choice but to go down further.
  • They wander the place until they found wast space with what it seemed to be a ger (Yurt) in the middle and behind that was a dozen branch people1 facing the sky. they travel through the crowd and Agent Olson loses two agents among them.
  • Agent Olson talks about the fairy tale that Agent Ouyulan told him. Saying that it isn't a small child fairy tale but a prophecy and the shepherd boy will reunite with his people when the prophecy is fulfilled.
  • the body cam began to sink into the ground and dragged above the surface, and we see the recovery team picking up the camera.

Hook/Attention: I decided to change the central narrative completely.

Footnotes
1. they are stationary and can’t move
